source_inventory.source_title: State of New Jersey v. Francisco Arteaga (A-3078-21)
source_inventory.relevance_note: Authoritative record of the first no-match search, subsequent NYPD RTCC possible match, construction of photo arrays, two eyewitness identifications, charges, partial facial-recognition discovery production, denial of the remaining eleven requested categories and appellate reversal requiring production.
source_inventory.evidence_status_basis: Published New Jersey appellate opinion directly establishes the investigative and discovery sequence, the material withheld evidence categories and the appellate disposition for which it is cited.
source_inventory.interpretive_reliance: Primary source for both the facial-recognition evidentiary chain and the material primary-evidence accessibility failure. It is not treated as a judicial finding that Arteaga was misidentified, wrongfully arrested or wrongfully detained.
source_inventory.deployment_context: New Jersey criminal investigation and prosecution using NJROIC and NYPD RTCC facial-recognition processes, followed by litigation over access to the underlying FRT evidence.
source_inventory.model_or_algorithm: NJROIC and NYPD RTCC facial-recognition systems; specific vendor/model details were among the contested discovery material

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct text review of the same court judgment through its public Justia PDF mirror; court-origin retrieval failed.
limitations: Opinion reviewed at investigation, witness and discovery holdings. It does not determine identity correctness or establish completed production after remand.

episode_inventory.source_paraphrase: A November 2019 store robbery produced surveillance footage. The victim saw the robbery; the manager described an earlier visit and later reviewed the footage.
NJROIC found no match; a later NYPD RTCC search offered Arteaga as a possible match.
episode_inventory.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A possible match remains an investigative lead.

episode_inventory.source_paraphrase: Investigators placed the returned photograph in two separate arrays with five fillers. The victim and manager each identified it in separate recorded interviews before indictment.
episode_inventory.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Separate interviews do not erase the common candidate-selection pathway.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The FRT result materially selected the identity shown to witnesses, but the two eyewitness identifications provide a separate evidentiary basis. Arteaga used an established criminal-discovery and appellate route to obtain non-public facial-recognition evidence needed to test the prosecution case. The existing route corrected the denial, but a production order does not establish realised governed access. The definition does not clearly locate an erroneous denial within an otherwise defined and reviewable pathway.

known_limitations: The published appellate opinion does not establish that the facial-recognition result was false, that Arteaga was innocent, or that his arrest or detention was wrongful.

The opinion records two eyewitness identifications after the NYPD RTCC supplied Arteaga as a possible match; VIGIL therefore does not treat the biometric inference as the sole or independently sufficient basis for the charge.

The reviewed authoritative evidence does not establish a duration of pretrial detention or a final disposition of the criminal prosecution, so the earlier registry-derived prolonged-detention severity claim is not retained as occurrence-level harm evidence.
review_history.review_outcome: Rebuilt and closed the Incident under the full-corpus campaign. Reclassified the occurrence from VIGIL-FC-000046 to VIGIL-FC-000044 Primary Evidence Accessibility Failure at high confidence: the State produced only part of the requested facial-recognition material, the trial court denied the remaining eleven discovery categories, and the Appellate Division reversed and ordered production because the material was directly relevant to testing FRT reliability, alternative suspects and reasonable doubt. FC-000046 was rejected because the possible FRT match was followed by two eyewitness identifications before Arteaga was charged. VIGIL-HIM was reduced from S4 to S3 because the authoritative record supports a meaningful but reversible procedural deprivation while the earlier prolonged-detention assertion remains uncorroborated.
